title: Formal sections comparison for the reduced structure sheaf
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for its maximal-ideal adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and of finite dimension. Let $I\subsetneq A$ be an ideal. For a finitely generated ideal $K$ of a ring $A$, write $H_K^j(M)=R^j\Gamma_K(M)$, where $\Gamma_K(M)=\{x\in M:K^nx=0\text{ for some }n\}$, and let $\operatorname{cd}(A,K)$ be the least integer $q\geq-1$ such that $H_K^j(M)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ and every $j>q$. Set $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $U=X\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$, and $Y=V(I)$. Put $B=A/\sqrt{(0)}$, let $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ be the quotient morphism, and write $V_{\rm red}=\pi^{-1}(V)$ for every open $V\subseteq U$. For $n\geq1$ let $T_n$ be the open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}(B/(IB)^n)$ lying over $U$. Let $d$ be the minimum of the dimensions of the irreducible components of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], with dimension understood as topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If $d>\operatorname{cd}(A,I)+1$, the canonical restriction homomorphism of rings $\varinjlim_{U\cap Y\subseteq V\subseteq U}\Gamma(V_{\rm red},\mathcal O)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\Gamma(T_n,\mathcal O)$ is an isomorphism. The colimit is over open neighborhoods ordered by reverse inclusion, with restriction maps, and the inverse limit uses reduction from $n+1$ to $n$.

source.place: Tag 0DXR (lemma-application-theorem), specialized to the coherent sheaf associated to A/sqrt(0); the complete-local application and reduced-structure-sheaf choice of Tag 0ECR (lemma-punctured-still-connected), first half of proof.

proof.text: Put $q=\operatorname{cd}(A,I)$, $N=\sqrt{(0)}$, and $M=B=A/N$, considered as an $A$-module generated by $1$. By [lem-per-local-cohomology-generator-bound], $q$ is a finite nonnegative integer: $I$ is finitely generated because $A$ is Noetherian, and $I$ is proper in the nonzero ring $A$. Since $A$ is local, $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-sbc-complete-local-subideal] to obtain $I$-adic completeness of $A$. These are the completeness and finiteness hypotheses needed below.

source.place: Tags 0DXR and 0ECR, preparation; algebra.tex Tag 090T, lemma-complete-by-sub.

proof.text: Check the depth alternative for $M$ in [lem-per-local-support-completion-comparison]. The quotient $B$ is reduced: if $b^r=0$ modulo $N$, any lift of $b$ has a power in $N$ and hence is nilpotent. It is Noetherian because every ideal lifts to an ideal of $A$, whose finitely many generators descend. Every prime of $A$ contains $N$, and chains of primes correspond to chains in $B$. If $\mathfrak p$ is minimal, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] gives $\dim\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)\geq d>q+1$, so the second alternative holds, since depth is nonnegative. Otherwise $\overline{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak p/N$ is nonminimal, so $\dim B_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}\geq1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-reduced], $\operatorname{depth}B_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}\geq1$. The surjection $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\overline{\mathfrak p}}=M_{\mathfrak p}$ carries the maximal ideal onto the maximal ideal; lifting a length-one regular sequence gives exactly the same injective multiplication map on $M_{\mathfrak p}$, and the same nonzero quotient. Thus $\operatorname{depth}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}\geq1$ by [def-weil-pbc-depth]. This verifies the alternative for every prime, in particular for all primes required by the comparison lemma.

source.place: Tag 0DXR, lemma-application-theorem, s=1 depth condition of Tag 0DXQ; algebra.tex Tag 031R, lemma-criterion-reduced.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-local-support-completion-comparison] to the finite $A$-module $B$, with the integer $q$ from step 1 and the depth alternatives checked in step 2. Obtain $J_0$ with $V(J_0)\cap Y=\{\mathfrak m\}$ and the isomorphisms $H^j(\alpha_J)$ for $j=0,1$ for every $J\subseteq J_0$ with $V(J)\cap Y=\{\mathfrak m\}$. Put $V_0=X\setminus V(J_0)$; then $U\cap Y\subseteq V_0\subseteq U$.

source.place: Tag 0DXP, lemma-algebraize-local-cohomology, s=1, used in the proof of Tag 0DXQ.

proof.text: For an open neighborhood $U\cap Y\subseteq V\subseteq V_0$, choose an ideal $J^\prime$ defining the closed set $X\setminus V$, and set $J=J^\prime J_0$. The identity $V(J^\prime J_0)=V(J^\prime)\cup V(J_0)=X\setminus V$ gives $J\subseteq J_0$, without assuming that an open determines a unique ideal. Since $V\subseteq U$ and $V$ contains $U\cap Y$, we have $V(J)\cap Y=\{\mathfrak m\}$ and $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-per-completed-affine-localization-diagram] with $M=B$. Its two exact rows compare $H_J^0(B)\to B\to\Gamma(V,\widetilde B)\to H_J^1(B)\to0$ and $H^0(C)\to B\to H^0(D)\to H^1(C)\to0$, where $C=(R\Gamma_{\mathfrak m}(B))^{\wedge_I}$ and $D=(R\Gamma(U,\widetilde B|_U))^{\wedge_I}$. The outside vertical maps are the isomorphisms of step 3 and the middle one is the identity of $B$.

source.place: Tag 0DXQ, theorem-algebraization-formal-sections, proof: localization triangles and comparison; choice of J made explicit.

proof.text: The exact rows in step 4 imply that $\beta_V:\Gamma(V,\widetilde B)\to H^0(D)$ is bijective. For injectivity, if $\beta_V(s)=0$, its boundary vanishes because $H^1(\alpha_J)$ is injective; write $s$ as the image of $b\in B$. The lower image of $b$ is zero, so $b$ comes from $H^0(C)$; surjectivity of $H^0(\alpha_J)$ lifts this preimage to $H_J^0(B)$, giving $s=0$. For surjectivity, take $t\in H^0(D)$. Lift its boundary via $H^1(\alpha_J)$, then lift that class to $s\in\Gamma(V,\widetilde B)$ using the top row. The boundary of $t-\beta_V(s)$ is zero, so this difference is the image of some $b\in B$. Adding the top image of $b$ to $s$ gives a preimage of $t$.

source.place: Tag 0DXQ, proof, the degree-zero exact-sequence argument after the two triangles.

proof.text: By [lem-per-punctured-derived-completion-sections], $H^0(D)=\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\widetilde{B/I^nB}|_U)$, with the natural reduction maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-tilde-spec] first to $A\to B$ and then to $A\to B/I^nB$: it identifies $\Gamma(V,\widetilde B)$ with $\Gamma(V_{\rm red},\mathcal O)$ and $\Gamma(U,\widetilde{B/I^nB})$ with $\Gamma(T_n,\mathcal O)$, since $I^nB=(IB)^n$. These identifications respect the ring structures and all maps: on a principal open $D(f)$, both take $b/f^r$ to the same fraction; reduction takes it to $(b\bmod I^nB)/f^r$. Equality on the principal-open basis gives equality of the sheaf maps and their restriction maps. The quotient sheaf has support in $U\cap Y\subseteq V$, so restriction from $U$ to $V$ is an isomorphism: extend by zero on the complementary open $U\setminus Y$ and glue on their overlap, where the quotient sheaf vanishes. By the open-subset clause of [lem-per-punctured-derived-completion-sections] for $V\subseteq U$, $H^0$ of the completed restriction $D\to(R\Gamma(V,\widetilde B|_V))^{\wedge_I}$ is the limit of these restriction isomorphisms, and completion on $V$ has the reduction coordinates. Therefore $\beta_V(s)$ has $n$th coordinate the unique section on $U$ extending $s\bmod I^nB$ on $V$, i.e. the restriction of $s$ to $T_n$. Consequently the bijection of step 5 is the canonical map to the stated formal-section ring, not an unspecified module isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0DXI, lemma-compare-with-derived-completion; Tag 0DXR applied to the reduced structure sheaf as in Tag 0ECR.

proof.text: Finally, the neighborhoods contained in $V_0$ are cofinal: replace any neighborhood $W$ by $W\cap V_0$. Each such neighborhood maps bijectively to the same inverse-limit ring by steps 5 and 6, compatibly with restriction. Explicitly, any element of the inverse limit is the image of a section on $V_0$, so the colimit map is surjective. If representatives on two neighborhoods have the same image, restrict them to their intersection with $V_0$; injectivity on that neighborhood makes their restrictions equal, hence their colimit classes equal. This proves injectivity. The canonical map preserves addition, multiplication and $1$ by restriction and reduction, so its bijectivity makes it an isomorphism of rings.

source.place: Tag 0DXR, passage from sufficiently small neighborhoods to the colimit; elementary representative argument.
